description: Pakistan's Interior Minister has held talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as part of mediation efforts to end the US-Iran conflict, amid signs that Tehran and Washington may be moving closer to an agreement. Eyre said the main issue is "sequencing", with Iran wanting to "front-load the benefits" before implementing the deal, while the US has the same concerns about trust. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
People in Syria's Deraa have celebrated death sentences handed down to former President Bashar al-Assad and senior members of his security apparatus over war crimes and crimes against humanity. They include Assad's cousin Atef Najib, the former head of political security in Deraa, who was accused of overseeing the brutal repression of protesters there in 2011. Assad and other senior officials fled to Russia after his government was overthrown in December 2024, making their extradition unlikely. Najib, who was arrested inside Syria, is among the few senior former regime officials likely to face the sentences. But the death penalty could complicate efforts to bring other officials to justice, as countries and international organisations generally do not cooperate with jurisdictions where defendants could face execution. 

Al Jazeera's Heidi Pett reports from Deraa.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Turkiye's parliament has approved legislation offering a conditional pardon to thousands of members of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), in a major step towards ending a four-decade conflict. The law allows some PKK-linked detainees to have prosecutions or prison sentences suspended for five to 10 years, with an initial release of around 3,500 people expected. Those convicted of killings and other serious offences would be excluded, as would the PKK's jailed founder Abdullah Ocalan. The legislation follows the PKK's decision to dissolve and disarm after Ocalan called for an end to its armed struggle in February 2025. The conflict began in 1984 and has killed more than 40,000 people, while spreading beyond Türkiye into Iraq, Syria and Iran. Supporters hope the law can help end decades of violence, but the government has made the process conditional and reversible. 

Al Jazeera's Sinem Koseoglu reports from Istanbul.
